# Editor Blocks — Full Documentation for AI Agents

> This file contains the complete text of the Editor Blocks documentation in a single
> retrievable document. It is the extended counterpart to `/llm.txt`.
>
> Editor Blocks is a library of ready-to-use, drop-in editor modules for React and Next.js.
> Modules are pre-tuned editor configurations for one job each, packaged the way shadcn/ui
> packages components: readable source you vendor and own.
>
> All shipped modules run on TipTap v3.31.4. The architecture reserves Lexical, ProseMirror,
> BlockNote, Slate, and Quill for future modules.

---

## 1. Overview

### What this is

Most projects end up building the same editor twice — once for a comment field, once for a
blog body — and the two implementations drift apart. Editor Blocks stops that. Each *module* is
a pre-tuned editor configuration for one specific job, with its extension set, toolbar, and
constraints already decided.

The name is deliberate: these are *blocks* you place, not a single editor you configure. Four
modules ship today. The contract is engine-agnostic so the catalogue can grow to cover other
editors without breaking.

### Design principles

1. **Modules, not frameworks.** You install a module that solves one job, not an entire editor
   framework you then configure.
2. **Engine-agnostic on purpose.** Each module declares which editor core powers it. Today that
   is TipTap. Others are reserved values, so adding an engine is a catalogue change rather than
   a rewrite.
3. **Copy the code.** Every module is readable source you can vendor into your own repository.
   No runtime lock-in, no black box.
4. **One contract.** All modules accept the same props and expose the same context API, so moving
   from a comment box to a full document editor is a one-word change.

---

## 2. Getting Started

### Requirements

| Tool      | Version                    |
| --------- | -------------------------- |
| Node.js   | 20.0.0 or newer            |
| npm       | 10.0.0 or newer            |
| React     | 19                         |
| Next.js   | 16 (App Router)            |

### Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/coderooz/Editor-Blocks.git
cd Editor-Blocks
npm install
npm run dev
```

The dev server starts on `http://localhost:3000`. If the port is busy, Next.js selects the next
free port and prints it.

### Scripts

| Command                | Purpose                                     |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`          | Start the dev server with hot reload        |
| `npm run build`        | Create an optimized production build        |
| `npm start`            | Serve the production build                  |
| `npm run lint`         | Run ESLint                                 |
| `npm run typecheck`    | Run the TypeScript compiler with `--noEmit` |

### Mount a module

```tsx
// app/comments/page.tsx
"use client";

import { EditorPage } from "@/components/EditorPage";

export default function CommentsPage() {
  return <EditorPage type="comment" />;
}
```

| `type` value   | Module                | Extension set           |
| -------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `"comment"`    | Comment Editor        | `COMMENT_EXTENSIONS`    |
| `"content"`    | Content Editor        | `BLOG_EXTENSIONS`       |
| `"document"`   | Document Editor       | `DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS`   |
| `"presentation"` | Presentation Editor | `PRESENTATION_EXTENSIONS` |

`EditorProvider` is already mounted in the root layout. Mounting a second provider on a page
creates a second editor instance and desynchronises the toolbar.

### Read and write content

```tsx
"use client";

import { useEditorContext } from "@/context/EditorContext";
import { EditorPage } from "@/components/EditorPage";

export default function ArticleEditor({ saved }: { saved: string }) {
  const { editorContent, charCount } = useEditorContext();

  return (
    <>
      <EditorPage type="content" initialContent={saved} />
      <p>Live HTML length: {editorContent.length}</p>
      <p>Character count: {charCount}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

**Security note:** the editor emits raw HTML. Sanitise with DOMPurify or `sanitize-html` before
persisting to a database or rendering on another domain. The editor does not sanitise on your
behalf.

---

## 3. API Reference

### `EditorPage` props

```tsx
interface EditorPageProps {
  /** Module id — selects the extension set and toolbar. */
  type: EditorType;
  /** Optional HTML seeded into the editor on first load. */
  initialContent?: string;
}
```

| Prop             | Type        | Required | Description                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ----------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`           | `EditorType`| Yes      | Selects the module. Changing it recreates the editor with that module's extensions and toolbar.   |
| `initialContent` | `string`    | No       | HTML applied when the editor becomes ready. Used to hydrate a saved draft.                        |

A page can mount exactly one editor: the shared provider holds a single instance, so nesting a
second `EditorPage` inside another will fight over state.

### `useEditorContext()`

```tsx
interface EditorContextValue {
  /** The live editor instance, or null before it is ready. */
  editor: Editor | null;
  /** Current module id. */
  editorType: EditorType;
  /** Switch module. Recreates the editor. */
  setEditorType: (type: EditorType) => void;
  /** Current HTML, updated on every keystroke. */
  editorContent: string;
  /** Seed or replace the HTML. */
  setEditorContent: (value: string) => void;
  /** Plain-text character count from the current document. */
  charCount: number;
}
```

| Field             | Type                          | Description                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `editor`          | `Editor \| null`              | Guard for `null` before calling chain commands. Null on first render pass.     |
| `editorContent`   | `string`                      | HTML string. Sanitise before persisting or rendering elsewhere.                 |
| `charCount`       | `number`                      | Length of the document's plain text. Differs from HTML length.                 |
| `setEditorType`   | `(t: EditorType) => void`     | Swaps the module. Destroys the current editor, losing content and undo history.|
| `setEditorContent`| `(v: string) => void`         | Seeds or replaces the document HTML.                                           |

### Extension presets

Exported from `constants/EditorExtension.tsx`:

```tsx
import {
  DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS,      // core building blocks
  COMPLEX_EXTENSIONS,      // DEFAULT + headings, tables, media, embeds
  BLOG_EXTENSIONS,         // alias of COMPLEX, for long-form content
  DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS,     // COMPLEX + CharacterCount (textSize)
  COMMENT_EXTENSIONS,      // DEFAULT + CharacterCount (limit 2500, nodeSize)
  PRESENTATION_EXTENSIONS, // COMPLEX + CharacterCount (textSize)
} from "@/constants/EditorExtension";
```

**Invariant:** register the link mark exactly once. `MarkdownLink` extends the stock `Link`
extension. Registering both yields two extensions named `link`, which TipTap warns about and
which breaks link input rules.

### Toolbar menu items

Toolbar items are plain data, grouped by category. Adding a button is an append, not a new
component.

```tsx
const MyButton: MenuItem = {
  title: "Strikethrough",
  group: "styling",          // controls the toolbar separator
  type: "button",
  icon: Strikethrough,
  isActive: (editor) => editor.isActive("strike"),
  action: (editor) => editor.chain().focus().toggleStrike().run(),
};
```

| `type`      | Renders          | Required fields                     |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `button`    | Icon button      | `title`, `group`                    |
| `dropdown`  | Select           | `title`, `group`, `options`, `onSelect` |
| `input`     | Text/colour input| `title`, `group`, `inputType`, `onSelect` |
| `model`     | Dialog           | `title`, `group`, `model`           |

**Invariant:** a toolbar button calls a command. If the matching extension is not in that
module's preset, the command does not exist and the click throws. Add the extension first.

### Utilities

```tsx
import { extractYoutubeId } from "@/lib/editor-utils";

extractYoutubeId("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"); // "dQw4w9WgXcQ"
extractYoutubeId("https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ");                 // "dQw4w9WgXcQ"
extractYoutubeId("not a url");                                    // null
```

---

## 4. Architecture

### Layers

| Layer     | Location                          | Responsibility                                        |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Routes    | `app/`                            | Mount a module by passing its id. No editor logic.    |
| Registry  | `constants/module-registry.ts`    | Authoritative module metadata. Drives every listing.  |
| Provider  | `context/EditorContext.tsx`       | Owns the single editor instance; resolves extensions. |
| Presets   | `constants/EditorExtension.tsx`   | Concrete TipTap extension arrays and menu definitions.|

### Request flow

1. A route renders `<EditorPage type="comment" />`.
2. `EditorPage` calls `setEditorType("comment")` in an effect.
3. The provider re-resolves extensions from its module → preset map.
4. `useEditor` is keyed on the module id, so a change tears down the old editor and builds a new one.
5. `EditorMenuBar` reads the module and selects its menu array.
6. `EditorContent` renders the ProseMirror surface.

**Trade-off:** step 4 is a full teardown. Switching modules discards content and undo history.
Capture `editorContent` before switching and pass it back as `initialContent` if you must
preserve it.

### Single instance model

`EditorProvider` is mounted once in the root layout. Everything reads the editor through context
rather than creating its own. One editor per page; a second provider would double state. The
editor is created with `immediatelyRender: false`, so there is no server/client markup mismatch.

### Registry as the single source of truth

Module metadata lives in exactly one file. Consumers:

```
app/modules/page.tsx               → cards, search, category filter
app/documentation/modules/page.tsx  → capability matrix
app/documentation/modules/[id]/     → one static page per module
app/documentation/page.tsx          → overview table
app/layout.tsx                     → JSON-LD structured data
public/llm.txt                     → machine-readable catalogue
```

This is why adding a module is a one-file change plus one route.

### Preset composition

```
DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS         core: doc, paragraph, text, basic marks, lists
  └─ COMPLEX_EXTENSIONS    + headings, tables, media, embeds, code blocks
       ├─ BLOG_EXTENSIONS         (alias)
       ├─ DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS     + CharacterCount (textSize)
       └─ PRESENTATION_EXTENSIONS + CharacterCount (textSize)

COMMENT_EXTENSIONS        DEFAULT + CharacterCount (limit 2500, nodeSize)
```

Higher tiers spread the ones below them, so a capability added to `DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS` appears
in every module. Add widely useful extensions low in the hierarchy rather than patching each
preset.

### Known trade-offs

| Decision                              | Consequence                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Module switch recreates the editor    | Content and undo history lost on switch. Acceptable for page-per-module.     |
| One shared provider in root layout    | A page cannot host two independent editors. Needs a scoped-provider refactor.|
| Presets are static arrays             | Extensions cannot be configured per host app without editing constants.     |
| Toolbar items are data, not components| Simple to extend, but bespoke JSX controls cannot be expressed yet.          |

---

## 5. Module Reference

### Comment Editor (`comment`)

Minimal TipTap editor for UGC surfaces: threaded comments, replies, review notes, feedback
forms. Ships only the formatting a commenter realistically needs and enforces a 2,500 character
ceiling so a comment cannot blow out a thread view.

- Tier: Minimal | Status: stable
- Best for: threaded comments and replies, review and approval notes, inline feedback widgets,
  quick-capture input
- Capabilities: bold, italic, underline, strike, links with autolink, bullet and ordered lists,
  blockquotes, inline code, live character count, 2500 character hard limit
- Extensions: Document, Paragraph, Text, Bold, Italic, Underline, Strike, Code, MarkdownLink,
  BulletList, OrderedList, ListItem, Blockquote, CharacterCount
- Live demo: `/examples/comment`
- Docs: `/documentation/modules/comment`

> The character limit is enforced via `CharacterCount`. Pasting longer content truncates it —
> split long input across multiple comments rather than raising the limit.

### Content Editor (`content`)

TipTap editor tuned for long-form publishing. Layers the comment baseline with the full
typography set — six heading levels, alignment, subscript and superscript, highlighting,
horizontal rules, and smart punctuation.

- Tier: Rich Content | Status: stable
- Best for: blog posts and articles, news and editorial content, CMS long-text fields, content
  marketing pages
- Capabilities: everything in Comment Editor, plus headings H1–H6 with Tailwind sizing, text
  alignment (left/center/right/justify), subscript and superscript, multi-colour highlight,
  horizontal rules, smart typography, font family / size / line height, text and background colour
- Extensions: Heading (custom per-level classes), TextAlign, Subscript, Superscript, Highlight,
  HorizontalRule, Typography, TextStyle, Color, BackgroundColor, FontFamily, FontSize, LineHeight
- Live demo: `/examples/content`
- Docs: `/documentation/modules/content`

### Document Editor (`document`)

The heaviest TipTap configuration. Adds syntax-highlighted code blocks, resizable tables,
collapsible details blocks, image drop-and-paste handling, YouTube embeds, and JSON
import/export, plus a textSize character counter.

- Tier: Full Featured | Status: stable
- Best for: documentation and wikis, knowledge bases, technical and legal writing, report
  authoring
- Capabilities: everything in Content Editor, plus syntax-highlighted code blocks (lowlight),
  resizable tables with header rows, collapsible details blocks, image insert / drop / paste,
  base64 image support, YouTube embed dialog, JSON import and export, character count (textSize)
- Extensions: CodeBlockLowlight, TableKit, Details, DetailsSummary, DetailsContent, Image,
  FileHandler, Youtube, CharacterCount
- Live demo: `/examples/docs`
- Docs: `/documentation/modules/document`

> The `Image` extension permits base64 sources, and the file handler accepts pasted and dropped
> images. Sanitise stored HTML before rendering it on another domain.

### Presentation Editor (`presentation`)

TipTap editor configured for presentation-shaped content. Reuses the full complex extension set
with a textSize character counter — suits slide copy, speaker notes, and structured walkthroughs
where heading hierarchy carries most of the meaning.

- Tier: Experimental | Status: beta
- Best for: slide decks and speaker notes, product walkthroughs, structured onboarding guides,
  course outlines
- Capabilities: everything in Content Editor, all complex block extensions, character count
  (textSize), heading-led structure
- Extensions: all complex extensions, CharacterCount (textSize)
- Live demo: `/examples/presentation`
- Docs: `/documentation/modules/presentation`

> Marked `beta`. The extension set may change between releases — pin the version if you depend
> on it in production.

---

## 6. Adding a Module

### Step 1 — define the extension preset

```ts
// constants/EditorExtension.tsx
import { CharacterCount } from "@tiptap/extensions";

export const TICKET_EXTENSIONS = [
  ...DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS,
  CharacterCount.configure({ limit: 8000, mode: "textSize" }),
];
```

### Step 2 — add the id to `EditorType`

```ts
// context/EditorContext.tsx
export type EditorType = "comment" | "content" | "document" | "presentation" | "ticket";
```

### Step 3 — map the id to the preset

```ts
// context/EditorContext.tsx — inside the provider
const map = {
  comment: COMMENT_EXTENSIONS,
  content: BLOG_EXTENSIONS,
  document: DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS,
  presentation: PRESENTATION_EXTENSIONS,
  ticket: TICKET_EXTENSIONS,   // ← new
} as const;
```

### Step 4 — register it in the catalogue

```ts
// constants/module-registry.ts
export const EDITOR_MODULES: EditorModule[] = [
  // …existing modules
  {
    id: "ticket",
    title: "Ticket Editor",
    summary: "Structured editor for support tickets with an 8,000 character budget.",
    description: "A TipTap editor sized for issue descriptions and support threads.",
    engine: "tiptap",
    engineVersion: "^3.31.4",
    category: "Rich Content",
    status: "beta",
    href: "/examples/ticket",
    docs: "/documentation/modules/ticket",
    extensionSet: "TICKET_EXTENSIONS",
    useCases: ["Support tickets", "Issue descriptions"],
    features: ["Everything in Comment Editor", "8,000 character budget"],
    extensions: ["All default extensions", "CharacterCount"],
  },
];
```

Then add a route at `app/examples/ticket/page.tsx`. The card, documentation page, search index,
structured data, and `llm.txt` all update automatically because they read from the registry.

### Adding a toolbar button

```tsx
import { Highlighter } from "lucide-react";

export const CONTENT_MENU: MenuItem[] = [
  // …existing items
  {
    title: "Highlight",
    group: "styling",
    type: "button",
    icon: Highlighter,
    isActive: (editor) => editor.isActive("highlight"),
    action: (editor) => editor.chain().focus().toggleHighlight().run(),
  },
];
```

### Adding a new engine

The `EditorEngine` type already reserves `lexical`, `prosemirror`, `slate`, `quill`,
`blocknote`, and `custom`. Wiring one up requires an adapter layer:

```ts
export interface EditorAdapter {
  getHTML(): string;
  setHTML(html: string): void;
  focus(): void;
  isEmpty(): boolean;
  destroy(): void;
}
```

The provider needs a branch that builds the adapter instead of calling `useEditor`. Keep the
adapter surface small so the context, toolbar, and counter stay engine-agnostic. Do not map a
non-Tiptap engine onto the TipTap command surface — if an engine cannot support a toolbar item,
omit the item rather than stubbing the command.

---

## 7. Roadmap

### Planned editor cores

| Engine      | Why it fits                                       | Trade-off                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Lexical     | Meta's editor, first-class React model, strong a11y | Different command API — needs the adapter layer first        |
| ProseMirror | The layer TipTap sits on; maximum control          | Verbose. Best reserved for schema-level control              |
| BlockNote   | Block-based model, closest to a document editor    | Own styling system; needs a theme bridge                     |
| Slate       | Flexible value model for custom inline behaviour   | Most work per module. Manual serialisation and normalisation |
| Quill       | Mature Delta format, small runtime, easy to embed  | Smaller extension ecosystem than TipTap                      |

These are reserved type values and design notes, not shipped work.

### Platform work

- **Publish the distributable package.** The `plugin/` scaffold holds extracted module sources.
  Publishing turns copy-paste into an npm install while keeping source access.
- **Per-host configuration.** Presets are static arrays today. An options-merge layer would let
  a host app adjust limits, allowed MIME types, and toolbar items without editing constants.
- **Multiple editors per page.** The shared provider holds one instance. A scoped-provider
  refactor would allow a comment box and a document editor on the same route.
- **Accessibility audit.** Toolbar semantics, focus restoration after dialogs, and contrast
  verification across the full extension set.
- **Test coverage.** Unit tests for the registry and the YouTube URL parser, plus end-to-end
  coverage of toolbar commands per module.

---

## 8. Repository Conventions

1. Module metadata lives in `constants/module-registry.ts` and nowhere else. Never hand-edit a
   page to list modules.
2. Module types are a string union (`EditorType`). Adding a value requires a matching entry in
   the provider's extension map, or it will compile but fall back to the default preset.
3. Source files carry an `@ai-agent` JSDoc tag describing non-obvious invariants. Read the
   header comment before changing a file.
4. Toolbar items are plain data grouped by category, not components.
5. The link mark must be registered exactly once (`MarkdownLink` replaces the stock `Link`).
6. Presets spread upward: add a widely useful extension to `DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS` rather than
   patching each tier.
7. Docs navigation lives in `constants/docs-nav.ts`.
